name: Micro Looper
description: An always-listening short looper: it loops what you just played as a soft bed, renews it as you play on, and can run the loop slower, lower, darker or backwards.

params.name: State
params.description: Listen only remembers what you play. Hold loops the last thing you played and keeps it for ever. Auto loops each new phrase in place of the last and lets it die away.

params.name: Length
params.description: How much of what was just played becomes the loop. Short lengths stutter on a fragment; long ones repeat a whole phrase.

params.name: Speed
params.description: How fast and which way the loop plays. Half is an octave down and twice as long, Double an octave up, and the Reverse settings run backwards. A change glides like tape.

params.name: Clock
params.description: The looper's own sample rate. Lower clocks record with less top, like an old sampler. Moved while a loop plays, it drops the loop by a fourth, a fifth or octaves.

params.name: Smear
params.description: Blends the plain loop into overlapping grains taken from around the same spot, which blurs the attacks and the point where the loop joins until it becomes a pad.

params.name: Fade
params.description: In Auto, how much of the loop is left after each time round. Low settings give a few fading repeats; at full the loop stays until the next phrase replaces it.

params.name: Drift
params.description: A slow random wobble in the loop's speed, and a slightly different starting point on each time round, so the loop never repeats quite the same way.

params.name: Tone
params.description: Takes highs off the loop so it sits behind what is played over it. The dry signal is not affected.

params.name: Spread
params.description: Widens the loop with two more reads from just ahead of and behind the playing point, one to each side. In mono they cancel, and the low end stays in the centre.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Balance between the dry signal and the loop.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. In outline a short always-listening looper with a variable sample clock, in the manner of small hold-style looper pedals: a ring buffer written and read at a divided clock with a band-limit that follows it, a loop join that is lined up where its two sides agree (a short cross-correlation search) and cross-faded by a law that follows how alike they are, and overlapping grains read around the loop position, after the approach of Curtis Roads, Microsound. Not a model of any particular unit.
